epoch_ai.synthesis: The Epoch Brief (Sept 12) rounds up Huawei's chip roadmap lagging Nvidia, GPT-6 Astra's benchmark records, and a new math benchmark; separately, their Aug 27 data insight tracks how fast Anthropic and OpenAI are actually growing revenue — the empirical bull-case data point behind the capex buildout debate.

semianalysis.synthesis: The on-thesis piece this week (Sept 15) disputes the 'moratoriums are killing the buildout' narrative with a parcel-level count: of ~20 GW sitting inside local restricted boundaries, only ~1.5 GW is actually delayed (three projects — an AWS campus in Ohio, a Pennsylvania powered-land site, one in Colorado), plus ~0.8 GW from New York's executive order. Their model still forecasts +38 GW of US datacenter IT capacity in 2027, more than double 2026, and argues Texas's ERCOT queue pause mostly pushes builders toward behind-the-meter generation rather than stopping them. Worth weighing against the Sept 14 farmdoc survey showing rural concern rising: SemiAnalysis's claim is that public opposition changes where and how capacity gets built, not how much.

ed_zitron.synthesis: Zitron's latest pushes back hard on a former Anthropic researcher's public 'AI could recursively self-improve, I'm scared' narrative, arguing the coverage anthropomorphizes model risk while sidestepping concrete, already-documented harms — consistent with his standing bear-case framing that AI-safety alarm often substitutes for AI-labor/AI-finance accountability. Note: the RSS feed's description field is not usable for synthesis (confirmed unreliable) — this is from the live article directly.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Indiana-relevant this week: the harvest-time low in corn basis lands in mid-October and runs deepest in Missouri, Indiana and Illinois (~16 cents below late-November on average at the state level), so selling off the combine carries a predictable discount (Sept 17). Illinois FBFM records from 1,927 farms show 2025 operator returns up in every region but still below the five-year average (Sept 18) — consistent with a squeezed-margin backdrop for land values. Also new: a Sept 21 piece on US vs. Argentine farmer perceptions of AI benefits.

data_center_dynamics.synthesis: Nothing Indiana/Midwest-specific again this week (Nokia AI-RAN, a subsea cable upgrade, LG cooling hardware). Second consecutive week with no on-thesis items — logged as a possible low-value pattern, not yet a cut.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana abnormally-dry (D0) coverage has risen for a third straight week: 0.1% (Sept 1) → 3.8% (Sept 8) → 8.7% (Sept 15), still with no D1 or worse. Small in absolute terms, but notable given Purdue Extension reported record August rainfall statewide — a fast dry-down after a wet month, worth watching into harvest.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Sept 13 (the week-ending Sept 20 numbers were still not in the NASS Quick Stats API as of Tuesday morning, so this is the latest available): Indiana corn 84% dented, 32% mature, 2% grain harvested; soybeans 43% dropping leaves, 3% harvested. Maturity jumped from 12% to 32% in one week — harvest is starting on a normal schedule.

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Unchanged for a third snapshot (Sept 12 → Sept 21): 56 tracked Indiana data-center projects, 33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational, led by Lake and Porter counties. Stable counts over ten days likely reflect how often interconnection.fyi updates its tracker, not a real pause.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: August 2026 was very wet in Indiana: 7.2 in. station-average precipitation, consistent with Purdue Extension's record-rainfall report, with temperatures near seasonal (73.0°F avg; highs 82.7°F, lows 63.3°F). Michigan: 68.0°F, 2.9 in. That wet month is the backdrop for the drought monitor's three-week rise in abnormally-dry coverage since.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Equitable Growth reposted a St. Louis Fed study (Bick, Blandin, Deming, Schumacher; Sept 8) that measures genAI use at work from a nationally representative survey, offering a direct adoption measure rather than exposure scores. A companion Sept 2 piece argues Unemployment Insurance gaps would leave many workers uncovered in an AI-driven disruption.

aspen_fsp.synthesis: Aspen FSP published 'Innovations to Accelerate Rural Wealth Building' (Sept 14), an interview-based report on rural wealth strategies — relevant to the democratization-of-capital thread — plus a Colorado 'Essential Wealth Metric' update estimating roughly two-thirds of Colorado households lack the wealth they need to thrive (Sept 11).

ipcc.synthesis: Administrative month: Annett Möhner named IPCC Secretary effective Nov 1, a co-sponsored expert meeting on water risk with IWMI, and review opening for the 2027 short-lived climate forcers methodology report. Nothing new on the AR7 timeline.
